Simulate future observations from parametric bootstrap refits

pb_predict_observations.Rd

Draws observation-level outcomes from the sampling model of each successful bootstrap refit, incorporating both fitted-model and process uncertainty.

Usage

pb_predict_observations(results, newdata, seed = NULL)

Arguments

results

A pb_boot object from pb_simulate or pb_parallel, fitted with keep_fits = TRUE.

newdata

Nonempty data frame of covariates for future observations.

seed

Optional seed for future response sampling, separate from the original bootstrap seed.

Details

Initially supported: unweighted Gaussian linear models, unweighted Poisson GLMs, and unweighted negative-binomial models fitted using MASS::glm.nb(). Gaussian observations are sampled using rnorm() with each refit's residual standard deviation; Poisson observations use rpois() and negative-binomial observations use rnbinom() with each refit's re-estimated theta. Binomial, mixed-effects, and Cox models, as well as non-unit case weights, are not supported by this function. The approach is model-conditional predictive simulation rather than an exact small-sample frequentist prediction interval.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per future observation and one column per successful bootstrap refit. Each entry is a newly sampled observation conditional on the corresponding refitted model.

See also

pb_predict_interval, pb_predict_boot

Examples

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
boot <- pb_simulate(fit, n = 30, seed = 1, keep_fits = TRUE)
new_cars <- mtcars[1:2, c("wt", "hp")]
draws <- pb_predict_observations(boot, new_cars, seed = 2)
dim(draws)
#> [1]  2 30
